title: Wendell and the Autopsy
premise: When the coffin of Harlan Voss, founder of the lakeside town of Meridian Falls, is exhumed for a land dispute, it proves empty — and hotel concierge Ulyana Nystrom, who has spent thirty years reading guests like weather, recognizes the exhumation order's handwriting as one they've seen on a guest register decades ago. As the sheriff's investigation stalls, Ulyana realizes the killer is someone who has been quietly curating the town's memory: forging records, coaching witnesses, and rewriting who Voss really was. Following a trail of small kindnesses and small cruelties through old ledgers, funeral receipts, and their own imperfect recollections, Ulyana discovers Voss never died — he vanished to escape his own crimes, and his protégé, the town archivist, murdered him years later when he threatened to return. In the flooded quarry where Voss was finally buried, Ulyana confronts the archivist, chooses truth over the town's comforting myth, and ends the case at the cost of Meridian Falls' founding story — and nearly their own life.
about_author: Theo Montrose is the pen name of a former night auditor who worked fifteen years in grand hotels across the Great Lakes region, collecting the confessions of insomniac strangers. They write mysteries about people whose jobs are to notice what others hope goes unseen.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty
chapters.summary: Ulyana Nystrom, concierge of the Hotel Meridian, watches from the lobby as the exhumation crowd returns from Hillcrest Cemetery. POV Ulyana. Beat: unease — the town's certainty cracks on day one.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dane Okonkwo questions Ulyana, who saw the gravediggers' faces change. Ulyana recalls every funeral they've staffed in thirty years. POV Ulyana. Beat: quiet pride in their memory turning to dread.

chapters.title: The Order in Familiar Ink
chapters.summary: Ulyana examines a copy of the exhumation order and freezes: the handwriting matches a 1989 guest register entry they've never forgotten. POV Ulyana. Beat: recognition — the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Founder's Day Ghosts
chapters.summary: Town prepares its centennial while gossip churns. Ulyana serves drinks to councilwoman Petra Voss-Ruud, the founder's great-granddaughter, and reads her grief as genuine. POV Ulyana. Beat: sympathy complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Perfect Files
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Elias Brandt, town archivist, whose records are immaculate — too immaculate. He quotes the case file verbatim before details were public. POV Ulyana. Beat: first cold spike of suspicion.

chapters.title: A Room Nobody Booked
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: 1991, a gaunt guest signing 'H. Vale' pays cash and asks Ulyana, then young, to hold letters. POV Ulyana (past). Beat: tenderness laced with foreboding.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Short List
chapters.summary: Sheriff Okonkwo shares suspects; Ulyana notices the file contains an error only someone inside could have planted. POV Ulyana. Beat: realization the killer is steering the investigation.

chapters.title: Petra's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Petra reveals the land dispute that forced the exhumation — and that someone anonymously tipped the surveyor. POV Petra. Beat: her loyalty to the family name beginning to fray.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana digs out the hotel's old ledgers and finds 'H. Vale' returned yearly until 2003 — then stops. POV Ulyana. Beat: obsession kindling; the pattern has a shape.

chapters.title: The Letters They Held
chapters.summary: Ulyana retrieves the sealed letters kept thirty years behind the front desk. One is addressed to Elias Brandt. POV Ulyana. Beat: guilt — they broke a promise by keeping them.

chapters.title: Elias Reads His Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana watches Elias open the letter; his face performs grief a half-second too late. POV Ulyana. Beat: the terrible intimacy of watching someone lie well.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: A diver searching the old Voss quarry for survey markers finds a boot sole instead. POV Okonkwo. Beat: the case turns criminal; the town holds its breath.

chapters.title: Who Benefits From a Myth
chapters.summary: Ulyana researches Voss's founding legend and finds contradictions — a fire, a missing partner, money that appeared from nowhere. POV Ulyana. Beat: disillusionment with the story the town tells itself.

chapters.title: Night Audit
chapters.summary: Someone searches Ulyana's office overnight; the 1991 register page is gone. POV Ulyana. Beat: violation — the killer knows exactly which memories matter.

chapters.title: Petra's Doubt
chapters.summary: Petra finds her grandmother's diary hinting Voss feared someone in town. She brings it to Ulyana, not the sheriff. POV Petra. Beat: alliance forming on shared doubt.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Remembered Wrong
chapters.summary: Deputy Sorrell's testimony shifts after a 'helpful' conversation with Elias. Ulyana catches the edit. POV Ulyana. Beat: anger — the killer isn't hiding, he's editing.

chapters.title: Vale, Again
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing dates, Ulyana concludes H. Vale was Harlan Voss alive all along, hiding in plain sight at their own hotel. POV Ulyana. Beat: vertigo — the truth sat at their desk.

chapters.title: What Voss Did
chapters.summary: The diary and ledgers converge: Voss's fortune came from a partner he ruined, and the fire killed the partner's son. POV Ulyana. Beat: horror — the beloved founder was the crime.

chapters.title: Threat in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Elias warns Ulyana gently to stop digging, framing it as protection of the town's peace. POV Ulyana. Beat: menace wrapped in kindness; fear takes root.

chapters.title: Okonkwo Closes the File
chapters.summary: Under political pressure, Okonkwo declares the empty coffin a clerical error. POV Okonkwo. Beat: defeat — institutions choosing comfort over truth.

chapters.title: Ulyana Alone With It
chapters.summary: Ulyana weighs letting the myth stand — their town, their hotel, their belonging against the truth. POV Ulyana. Beat: the book's moral hinge; loneliness.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Among the held letters, Ulyana finds one written in 2003: Voss announcing he was coming home to confess. POV Ulyana. Beat: motive revealed — someone needed him never to arrive.

chapters.title: Following the Funeral Money
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces 2003 burial expenses to an account administered by the historical society — Elias's domain. POV Ulyana. Beat: the net tightening; cold clarity.

chapters.title: Petra Confronts the Archive
chapters.summary: Petra requests the original founding documents; hours later the archive suffers a small 'electrical fire.' POV Petra. Beat: escalation — Elias is burning the past in real time.

chapters.title: Sorrell's Confession
chapters.summary: Deputy Sorrell admits Elias fed him the false timeline and breaks down. POV Sorrell. Beat: the edited witness unedited; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Okonkwo Reopens
chapters.summary: Armed with Sorrell's statement, Okonkwo reopens the case but warns Ulyana they're now a target. POV Okonkwo. Beat: reluctant partnership; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Ulyana reconstructs Voss's final visit week-by-week from housekeeping logs and bar tabs. POV Ulyana. Beat: elegy — they liked the lonely man named Vale.

chapters.title: Elias's Origin
chapters.summary: Interleaved documents reveal Elias was the ruined partner's grandson, raised on grievance, hired by Voss himself without knowing. POV Elias (documents/diary). Beat: tragic symmetry — the avenger adopted by his enemy.

chapters.title: The Quarry Meeting
chapters.summary: Ulyana baits Elias with a forged letter claiming Voss left a full confession in the hotel safe. POV Ulyana. Beat: the hunter becomes bait; terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Empty Safe
chapters.summary: Elias comes for the safe at 3 a.m.; Ulyana and Okonkwo wait — but Elias anticipated the trap and cut the power. POV Ulyana. Beat: trap inverted; darkness both literal and moral.

chapters.title: Catwalk Over the Lobby
chapters.summary: In the blackout, Elias corners Ulyana above the lobby, speaking almost lovingly about the town they both served. POV Ulyana. Beat: climax begins — two keepers of memory, opposite verdicts.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Remembers
chapters.summary: Ulyana stalls him with the one thing he can't edit: their eyewitness memory of Vale's face, voice, and final request. POV Ulyana. Beat: memory as weapon and mercy.

chapters.title: Petra at the Door
chapters.summary: Petra arrives with the recovered diary pages and names Elias before the sheriff's lights flood the lobby. POV Petra. Beat: witness restored; the circle closes.

chapters.title: Falling Man
chapters.summary: Elias bolts across the catwalk; Okonkwo takes a knife wound stopping him. He surrenders not from defeat but because Ulyana says his grandfather's name aloud. POV Okonkwo. Beat: climax resolves — truth disarms where force couldn't.

chapters.title: Confession in the Archive Ruins
chapters.summary: Elias recounts the 2003 quarry killing in devastating detail, insisting he buried Voss 'where the town wouldn't have to look.' POV Elias. Beat: chilling calm; evil convinced of its own tidiness.

chapters.title: The Town Hears It All
chapters.summary: The confession becomes public; Founder's Day collapses into reckoning. Some residents turn on Ulyana for breaking the myth. POV Ulyana. Beat: cost of truth — belonging wounded.

chapters.title: Petra's New Plaque
chapters.summary: Petra commissions a truthful historical marker naming the partner and his son. POV Petra. Beat: grief transmuted into repair.

chapters.title: Room 214
chapters.summary: Ulyana reopens Room 214, Vale's old room, and finally reads the last letter aloud — Voss asking forgiveness no one owed him. POV Ulyana. Beat: mourning the man and the monster together.

chapters.title: The Register, Restored
chapters.summary: Ulyana re-enters the lost 1991 page from memory, signing it as witness. Okonkwo closes the case properly. POV Ulyana. Beat: restoration — memory honored, not mythologized.

chapters.title: Concierge, Still Noticing
chapters.summary: Spring at the Hotel Meridian: new guests, old scars, Ulyana at the desk reading everyone like weather — now including themselves. POV Ulyana. Beat: resolution — belonging rebuilt on truth, quieter and real.
